# Philip Rubin: A Multifaceted Leader in Science, Policy, and Arts
Philip Rubin is a distinguished psychologist, scientist, administrator, and artist whose career, spanning from the 1970s to the 2020s, encompasses computational linguistics, behavioral science, and technology policy. Academically, he is renowned for his work on embodied cognition, articulatory synthesis (including the ASY and CASY systems), and sine-wave speech synthesis, utilizing a dynamical systems perspective to understand speech perception, production, and the vocal tract.
His leadership roles include serving as President of the Federation of Associations in Behavioral and Brain Sciences (FABBS), Chairman of Haskins Laboratories, and holding emeritus status at iGIANT. In government and policy, Rubin held significant positions at the National Science Foundation (NSF) and the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP), where he directed behavioral sciences divisions, championed open science, and advocated for academic freedom and public trust in research institutions. He has also contributed to federal and state efforts by serving on the NASA Advisory Council, the University of Connecticut's Board of Trustees, and as a judge for the DARPA Robotics Challenge.
Rubin is equally active in education and advocacy, supporting STEM through RISE (NSF/IBM) and the Franklin Institute's Bower Award, while chairing the National Academies Board on Behavioral Sciences and co-founding the IS Group. Known for his critical stance on emerging technologies, he has publicly challenged initiatives such as the TSA's SPOT program and questioned the efficacy of voice stress detection. He is also a vocal advocate for scientific integrity and public health, notably signing an Open Letter to postpone the 2016 Rio Olympics due to the Zika virus.
Beyond his scientific achievements, Rubin is a Fellow of prestigious organizations including the APA, AAAS, and the Acoustical Society of America, having received the White House OSTP Award for Excellence and the iGIANT Pioneer Award. His diverse interests extend into the arts; born in 1949, he is a photographer specializing in urban wall art and a musician who co-founded the band The Institution in the mid-1960s. He remains active in the alternative art scene, notably featured in *Mineshaft* magazine, and collaborates with musicians who utilize his pioneering speech synthesis technology. Married to Joette Katz, he is the father of Dr. Jason Wilder Katz Rubin and Samantha Katz.
